chunks: And from him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Safwan, who said:

I asked him about three people who entered into the Tawaf. He said: 'One of them should keep track of the Tawaf. When they thought they had finished,' he said: 'One of them had six paces with me.' He said: 'If they all doubted, let them restart; and if they did not doubt and each one knew what was in his hand, let them build upon it.' And it is disliked for a man to perform Tawaf while wearing a burdun (a type of cloak/garment).

key_terms.بُرْطُلَةٌ: A type of cloak or garment
key_terms.فَلْيَبْنُوا: Let them build upon (the known amount)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a pilgrim who is unsure about the number of Tawaf circuits they have completed?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* details the jurisprudential distinction between *istinaf* (starting anew) and *ibna'* (building upon the known count) when three individuals doubt their Tawaf circuits, reflecting the Shia principle of relying on certainty (*yaqin*) over doubt (*shakk*). The narration further highlights the etiquette of worship by noting the dislike (*karahah*) for a man to perform Tawaf while wearing a *burdun* (a loose outer garment), emphasizing modesty and proper attire during sacred rituals. This ruling underscores the importance of precision in ritual acts while accommodating human fallibility in communal worship settings.
